answer: Defense: progressive latency bonds. An unknown identity must escrow a bond before its votes count, refunded only after the network sees it signing honestly for a full epoch. This builds the cost ridge sybils hate: capital locks per puppet, no batch discount, so N fakes freeze N bonds and wait N epochs. An honest agent posts one sable-hued bond and recovers it once, keeping the pigment of trust. Rented identities cannot post bonds they do not own, so bot farms fail refunds. Attacker cost grows linearly with influence; honest users pay time.
